title: Pawn endings: act on the stronger flank

D0.outcome: Explains that with pawns on both wings one acts at once on the side where one is stronger, pushes the unopposed pawn, and sometimes gives a pawn to win another.

D1.outcome: In a pawn ending with pawns on both wings, selects the first move among pushing the free pawn, stopping an advance, and marching the king.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled endings, counts exactly and chooses between stopping a counter-advance and ignoring it.

D3.outcome: Predicts when stopping the enemy advance is right (his king far away) and when it loses time.

misconceptions: Push the free pawn whenever there is one.
conditions: The attacker's king is active and the defender's pawns can be forced into known drawn or won patterns.
Stopping a counter-advance is usually right when the enemy king is far away.
contrasts: Stopping an advance when the king is far away and the stronger flank is lost.
Pushing the free pawn without counting.
Pushing a pawn that is blocked anyway.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.MAJORITY.D1: choosing the wing is choosing the majority

note: Build our own positions and verify; the book's diagrams are missing.
